newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-RBA sees falling Australian bank profits.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-RBA sees falling Australian bank profits.

text.p: Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) Governor designate Ian Macfarlane said on Thursday increased competition in mortgage lending had cut bank margins almost in half in the last three years and was likely to cut bank profits.
Macfarlane said the Reserve Bank welcomed this trend of increased competition cutting profits.
"It's (the competition) reduced the margins on housing lending from over four percent to a little bit over two percent over the last three or four years," Macfarlane said.
"It's clearly is going to reduce bank profits," he said.

"So it is working and when that starts to show through in the full year figures we will clearly see a reduction in margins and probably a reduction in profits and we're very happy with that," he said.
The entrance of mortgage originators had lifted competition amoung banks to new levels and the Reserve Bank welcomed that.
"When we look ahead and see what is happening, we welcome that, we see competition working and we welcome it," he said.
Three of the four dominant banks in Australia have years ending September 30 and are due to report full year results later this year.
Most of the major banks have forecast flat to slow profit growth.
